summary: Views get a strong self-handle: Context.StrongSelf() returns the view's own Entity[S] for listener capture during Render, mirroring the reference Context::entity (strong in Rust through clone-owned ref counts). The lease behind it is retained once per (window, view) in the rendering window's scope, shared by every later read, and releases deterministically at window close — the conforming adaptation of the reference's closure-owned strong handle under the recorded ownership contract (Context.Entity stays a callback-borrowed facade; saving an owned handle requires RetainInto, and facades do not leak one owned lease per render). OpenWindowView now builds the root view with the window as the active frame-construction boundary (the reference open_window window_update_stack), so the root placement's ViewOf lease is the window's and closes with it instead of leaking to the app root scope until shutdown.

deviations: Context.Entity() remains a callback-borrowed facade (the recorded ownership decision); the ticket's first option (Entity() retaining an independent lease) conflicts with that recorded contract, so the ticket's second option — the window-owned strong self-handle read in Render — is the implemented conforming pattern.

The reference's listener closures own strong Entity clones released when the element tree drops them; Go has no closure-drop release, so the window's scope owns ONE shared lease per (window, view) instead of one lease per captured closure. The observable difference: a view stays alive until its window closes even if a placement stops rendering mid-window (upstream would drop the subtree's closures at the next frame build); leases never accumulate per render.

The self-handle facade is never expiring but not owned by the caller: Release/TransferInto panic with the window-ownership diagnostic; RetainInto supplies an independently owned copy and Downgrade a weak identity, matching DowncastView's facade precedent.

A view entity rendered by two windows holds one self-handle lease per window (plus each window's placement lease): closing one window leaves the other working; the last close releases the view when no independent owner remains.
